title: One thing that always bothered me about life sims is that after a while you've basically seen every event.
author: YuewenGame
selftext:
I started experimenting with AI to generate more life stories, careers, random encounters and small moments.Not because I think AI can replace game design.Mostly because I'm one guy and there's no way I can write thousands of events myself.Maybe it's a terrible idea.Maybe it'll make the game feel more alive.

I'm still figuring that out.

comments.author: Prophysaon_Coeruleum
comments.body: It’s a very tough problem to solve. Wiring up an LLM to your game is not that hard. Getting it to understand context and generate interesting content without being an expensive RNG on the other hand…

replies.author: YuewenGame
replies.body:
I agree with this point. What players are most worried about is not AI being involved in content generation, but rather a world where “everything is generated by AI with no human design intent behind it.”

However, if the rules are designed by humans, and AI is only used to make each life experience richer and more unpredictable, people are much more likely to accept it.

By the way, I’ve been working on a project https://store.steampowered.com/app/4798150/Life_Memoirs/Well recently — a life simulation game about the life of an ordinary person in China. While building it, I found it quite interesting how different choices can lead to very different life trajectories.

comments.author: HLCYSWAP
comments.body:
instead of putting llm anywhere near a videogame use it to write the thousands of encounters. feed it a json of what you already have and use that with a prompt similar to 'write 100 events for this in the same style. do not repeat any events. report outside of json similarity cosine % to any seen events'

  
approve what it outputs, tweak it, then refeed it back and and go again until you have a number you like
